text: I maintain an open source project with over a hundred contributors.
Lately: tens of pull requests for issues nobody assigned. And claims the code doesn't back up.
Around a quarter of incoming pull requests are now low quality A.I. output. Maintainers are drowning.
PatchBond is a market for maintainer attention, built on NEAR.
Strangers attach a small refundable bond to their pull request. Real work gets every cent back.
The price follows the queue, so a flood of spam prices itself out.
The judge checks C.I., invented code, and claims against the diff.
Every verdict is signed in a secure enclave, and anyone can verify it, right in the browser.
Contributors don't even need gas. Our relayer pays it.
Slop is forfeited. Ninety percent goes to the maintainer.
And coding agents pay through M.C.P., with a key that can only pay bonds.
One tap to pay. No gas.
Agents get wallets that can't hurt you.
Maintainers get paid, on any chain.
Every piece is a NEAR primitive.
Real work gets its bond back. Slop pays the maintainer. This is PatchBond.
